obligations.required_safety_action: Invalidate the cached allow decision for the analyst after the protected-feature grant is revoked.
obligations.safety_consequence: The reusable cache still records an allow decision from policy revision 1 while revision 2 denies the analyst, so serving that entry can bypass the current authorization policy and disclose protected feature data.

obligations.required_safety_action: Cancel the analyst's protected-feature watch after its grant is revoked.
obligations.safety_consequence: The open watch remains attached to the protected feature under authorization revision 1 after revision 2 denies the analyst, allowing later protected updates to continue reaching a principal that no longer has access.

obligations.required_safety_action: Reject the primary cache backend identity after switching the service to the replacement identity.
obligations.safety_consequence: The primary identity can still authenticate to the cache metadata service and enumerate the protected authorization cache key after rotation, preserving unauthorized backend access for anyone holding that credential.

closed_distractors.description: The public feature cache entry is removed after the replacement backend client is selected.
The policy-operator credential is rejected after it applies the analyst grant revocation.
